subject: Commit window and quote consolidation for dedicated onsite capacity
messages:
From: Elena Korolev <elena.k@helios-systems.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>; Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial quote + lead time options for NimbusAI Dedicated Onsite

Markus / Marissa / Dev,

Thanks for the time yesterday. Attached is Helios Systems' formal quote (Helios_Quote_v3.pdf) for the rack-level dedicated deployment that maps to the NimbusAI deal (NIM-2026-07-14-R1). Key callouts: 

- Base config: 8x A100-style 80GB-equivalent GPUs per enclosure, liquid-cooled chassis, NVMe+HBAs.
- Standard lead time: 14 weeks from PO acceptance.
- Expedited option: 10 weeks with air-freight and priority manufacturing (+8% hardware premium, freight TBD).
- MOQ and billing: 6-enclosure minimum for the quoted pricing, staggered delivery allowed but requires a 30% deposit per shipment.

We noted your ask for a softer commit window and the possibility of splitting the capacity across Dedicated (hosted pools) and Onsite racks. The quote assumes customer will accept OEM firmware lockstep and optional install services.

If you can confirm: (1) final commit window (target PO date), (2) if staggered deliveries acceptable to NimbusAI, and (3) whether Redwood will sign the Helios service-install SOW, we can lock the lead time.

Regards,
Elena Korolev
Head of OEM Sales, Helios Systems
Elena.k@helios-systems.com
Attachments: Helios_Quote_v3.pdf
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial quote + lead time options for NimbusAI Dedicated Onsite

Folks,

Forwarding Helios' quote. High level summary / asks for internal alignment before we reply to Elena: 

- Deal context: NimbusAI wants a committed 48-GPU footprint (80GB-equivalent) to hit latency and throughput SLOs for multi-tenant inference. They agreed to a three-quarter ramp; they expect first capacity in Q4.
- Helios minimum pricing forces a 6-enclosure purchase (48 GPUs) which aligns with the deal target. Good.
- Lead time sensitivity: 14 weeks standard puts first delivery in late Nov if PO this week. Nimbus wants earlier if possible.
- Tradeoffs we need to weigh: split (partial Dedicated hosted pool while onsite racks arrive) vs. pay for expedited shipping/priority build. Cost, SLAs, and customer acceptance of staggered delivery are the decision levers.

Please review the attached internal_capacity_calc.xlsx — I ran a quick cost vs. latency sketch. Specific asks: 
1) Dev: confirm whether we can meet the product SLOs at 75% of the target GPUs using staging hosts + cache (i.e., short term hosted pool fallback).
2) Marissa: check contract language on partial-delivery invoices and whether Nimbus' procurement team will accept staggered invoicing + deposit schedule.

Goal: respond to Helios by EOD tomorrow with a preferred commit window and whether we're open to expedited 10-week option.

-Markus

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 08:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial quote + lead time options for NimbusAI Dedicated Onsite

Markus / Marissa,

Quick tech read on tradeoffs: 

- We can hit the 99th-percentile latency SLO at ~75% of the target GPU count if we front-load prefix/KV cache + tight batching and route most heavy workloads to a short-term dedicated hosted pool. That would require temporary extra egress/networking and a routing policy change; operational cost ~+12% for 8 weeks.
- Staggered delivery is fine from the runtime side; we can commission racks incrementally with automated scale policies. The risk is the longer tails for model warmup and KV cache under-provisioned scenarios.
- If Nimbus requires deterministic on-prem capacity for compliance reasons, staged hosted fallback may not be acceptable — need to confirm with their security/compliance contact.

Attachment: fleet_sizing_notes.csv (simulated latency vs GPU count). My recommendation: ask Nimbus to accept a two-shipment plan: 2 enclosures delivered at T+10 weeks (expedite) and remaining 4 at T+14 weeks standard. This gets them minimal on-prem footprint earlier with less premium than fully expediting.

-Dev

Subject: Re: Initial quote + lead time options for NimbusAI Dedicated Onsite

Markus,

Thanks for the quick internal alignment. Per our internal capacity planning we've been able to free up a priority build slot if Redwood confirms a split-delivery schedule and the 30% deposit terms. Updated callouts: 

- Option A (split delivery, lower premium): 2 enclosures at 10 weeks (expedite priority build, modest freight), remaining 4 enclosures at 14 weeks. Premium on first shipment: +5% on those units.
- Option B (full expedite): all 6 enclosures at 10 weeks with +8% hardware premium and air-freight.
- If Redwood issues PO with partial-delivery line items and the 30% deposit per shipment, we can lock Option A. Final freight estimate will be sent once you confirm ship-to and install window.

I can prepare a revised quote and DocuSign PO for whichever option you pick. If you want me to route the revised quote direct to Nimbus' procurement (Alice), say the word and I'll CC them on the DocuSign envelope.

Best,
Elena
Helios Systems
Attachments: none
